Article Title: 'Rubbing salt into Pahalgam victims' wounds': Row over Pakistan minister at SCO meet in Delhi
Article Text:
Congress leaders criticised the Centre over Pakistan minister Masood Malik's visit to Delhi for the SCO Civilisation Dialogue

NEW DELHI: A political row broke out after Pakistan minister Masood Malik arrived in Delhi on Friday to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue. Congress questioned the invitation and accused the BJP-led Centre of “rubbing salt into the wounds of Pahalgam victims’ families”."You keep changing your stance. Sometimes you travel there, sometimes you reach Lahore, at other times you abruptly call off Operation Sindoor, and now you invite them here. What exactly is Prime Minister Modi doing? The funeral pyres of those martyred in the Pahalgam massacre have not even cooled yet, and you are rubbing salt into the wounds of their families,” said Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate."The Government of India, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is organising the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in India on November 21 and 22. The question is: why was Pakistan invited to this event? Why have you invited Pakistan, a country that sponsors terrorism in India? You invited Pakistan, and its minister, Musadik Malik, has arrived here," she said.Questioning the "red carpet" treatment being extended to the minister, Shrinate said, "This is the same person who had openly threatened just a few months ago to chop off the hands of Indians and shed our blood.""The question is that Pakistan has not stopped sponsoring terrorism, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is busy welcoming its representatives. Musadik Malik be served biryani, kebabs and kheer? The government is rolling out the red carpet to welcome him. Why does your work not get done without an anti-India Pakistan? The point is that you should also say and do what Rahul Gandhi has stated unequivocally: as long as Pakistan continues to sponsor terrorism, no dialogue with it is possible," she added.J&K Congress President Tariq Hameed Karra also accused the BJP of having "double standards" regarding militancy, Indo-Pakistan talks, or international treaties."Look, as far as the Government of India is concerned, particularly the BJP,ey have always had double standards. Whether it is regarding militancy, Indo-Pakistan talks, or international treaties, their approach has consistently been marked by double standards. The very person who made the loudest protests when the Indus Waters Treaty was suspended here had raised more objections than anyone else at that time. But the fact that they are displaying double standards is nothing new," he said."This is another example of their double standards. When our Prime Minister went to Pakistan uninvited, what could be a bigger example of double standards than that? Basically, the BJP has lost its track.Its foreign policy is being handled on a day-to-day basis. It has no consistent or permanent policy towards its neighbouring countries, whether Pakistan, China, Bangladesh or Sri Lanka. They deal with each country according to what suits them at a particular time," he added.Pakistan's federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination Masood Malik arrived in New Delhi to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue. He was received by Pakistan high commissioner's Chargé d'Affaires in India, Saad Warraich. Malik's visit marks the first time a Pakistani minister has travelled to India in three years.
Article Summary: Congress leaders criticised the Centre over Pakistan minister Masood Malik's visit to Delhi for the SCO Civilisation Dialogue. Congress accused the BJP-led Centre of “rubbing salt into the wounds of Pahalgam victims’ families”

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has permitted the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, on November 24, 2026, as an interim arrangement.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi, however, stayed portions of the Madras high court judgment that had upheld the direction to restore the practice of lighting the lamp at the Deepathoon. The interim permission comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah over ownership of the hilltop and the location of the ritual.The development follows arguments by the dargah before the top court on Thursday, when it claimed ownership of the entire hilltop and opposed the demand to light the lamp at the stone pillar. The hearing on the matter had remained inconclusive, with the court scheduled to continue proceedings on Friday.Senior advocate Amit Anand Tiwari, appearing for the dargah, referred to a 1920 judicial order passed in a civil suit and said there were findings establishing that the flight of stairs from Nellithope to the hill belonged to the shrine."The entire top of the hill belongs to the dargah. There is no question of lighting the deepam at the top of the hill, where the stone pillar is situated, irrespective of what the distance between the dargah and the stone pillar is," Tiwari said.He also submitted that the "whole of the top of the hillock on which the mosque and the flagstaff stand" as well as the stone pillar are located is the property of the dargah.The controversy centres on the location of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lighting ceremony at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple in Thiruparankundram. For decades, the festival lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes of the hill.Hindu groups have sought permission to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone pillar higher up the hill and around 50 metres from the dargah. The dispute has led to legal proceedings over the location of the ritual and ownership of the hill.The Tamil Nadu government had opposed the demand, arguing that permitting the lighting of the lamp near the dargah could create wider legal and administrative complications. On Wednesday, it told the Supreme Court that allowing the practice could lead to thousands of survey pillars across the country acquiring a religious character.The dargah committee had also challenged the procedure followed by the Madras High Court. Senior advocate Huzefa Ahmadi, appearing for the committee, argued that a single-judge bench had passed its order without giving the dargah adequate time to file a reply under the high court rules. He also submitted that the judge had conducted a site visit without notifying the dargah before passing the order.The Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department has opposed a petition seeking to bring the temple and the entire Thiruparankundram hill under the control of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).In an affidavit before the Supreme Court, HR&CE Commissioner T G Vinay said the temple's ownership and existing religious practices had been settled through decades of judicial proceedings. He maintained that the hill was owned by the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple to the extent recognised by a civil court decree of 1923, which was subsequently restored by the Privy Council in 1931.The affidavit opposed three reliefs sought by petitioner Hindu Dharma Parishad: handing over the entire temple and hill to the ASI, keeping a lamp burning round the clock at the stone pillar described as the Deepathoon, and illuminating the entire hill with lamps during Karthigai Deepam."A title so settled cannot be disturbed and the administration of a religious endowment entrusted by statute to the HR&CE cannot be wrested away and handed over to the ASI upon a petition that pleads no ground in law and seeks the relief in the teeth of a concluded civil adjudication of title," the affidavit had said.On the lighting ceremony, the HR&CE commissioner maintained that the festival lamp had traditionally been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple, and not at the hilltop or the stone pillar.The department also referred to historical records of attempts made in 1862 and 1912 to light lamps near the hill's summit, where the dargah is situated. It argued that archaeological protection at Thiruparankundram covered specified features, including the rock-cut cave and inscriptions, and did not extend to the entire hill or the functioning temple.The department cautioned that allowing lamps to be lit at multiple locations, particularly near the dargah, could disrupt existing arrangements and create law-and-order challenges at a site with a history of communal tension.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has permitted the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. The interim permission comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah. The dispute has led to legal proceedings over the location of the ritual and ownership of the hill.

Article Title: Operation Monsoon Thunder: NCB raids four cities, arrests six in probe into US-bound opioid and psychotropic drug shipments
Article Text:
Arti Soni, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh/ Abdul Muttalib @ Rocky @ Monio Kolkata, West Bengal/ Talabathula Manoj Allapur, Hyderabad

New Delhi: In a sweeping international crackdown, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) have dismantled the Indian nerve center of a massive transnational drug syndicate — shutting down an illicit pipeline flooding American streets with deadly opioids and psychotropic substances.​Under an operation code named, Monsoon Thunder, NCB teams carried out raids across multiple Indian cities —including Hyderabad, Delhi, Kolkata, and Lucknow — resulting in the arrest of six individuals linked to the network.The raids were carried on Nov 4 and Nov 13. According to investigative findings, the syndicate operated across borders to supply controlled drugs to buyers throughout the United States.Digital records and examined evidence indicate that the group handled nearly 3,000 parcels containing approximately five lakh tablets between June 2022 and November 2026.During the probe, NCB also flagged several active consignments holding more than 1,500 tablets bound for U.S. destinations and shared actionable intelligence with the DEA, which subsequently seized two shipment consignments.Investigators found that Indian operators took orders via encrypted and messaging platforms such as Telegram, Skype, and WhatsApp, while the U.S.-based arm dispatched shipments through postal and delivery networks, including the United States Postal Service (USPS).Consignment and buyer information was tracked in shared digital records, including Google Sheets. Authorities uncovered a vast customer database covering more than 59,000 subjects—containing transaction histories, past shipment details, delivery addresses, USPS tracking IDs, and drug types—which has been handed over to the DEA to support ongoing intelligence analysis and enforcement against U.S. buyers and drop-shippers.Financial probes show that Indian operators collected payments and commissions through multiple channels, including Venmo, UPI, cryptocurrency, third-party bank accounts, and hawala networks.Investigators are tracing these financial flows to identify ultimate beneficiaries and map illicit proceeds. Additionally, digital files and medicine brand details recovered from an arrested operative point to potential sourcing from several countries, prompting further investigation into procurement channels and international movement.NCB officials said the operation highlights ongoing efforts to counter syndicates abusing digital tools, postal systems, and cross-border supply chains for illicit pharmaceutical trafficking, reaffirming commitment to coordinated international enforcement against narcotic and psychotropic drug networks.
Article Summary: Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) have dismantled the Indian nerve center of a massive transnational drug syndicate. Under an operation code named, Monsoon Thunder, NCB teams carried out raids across multiple Indian cities. The raids were carried on Nov 4 and Nov 13.

Article Title: Old Monk maker Mohan Meakin, India’s largest rum maker, faces revenue setback after FSSAI questions the composition and labelling of three rum variants produced at its Maharashtra facility; revenue dr

India’s largest rum maker by volume, Mohan Meakin, which is known for its Old Monk has taken a serious revenue hit. The company saw its revenue more than halve in the first six months of the current financial year after food safety authorities stopped sales of three Old Monk variants which are produced at its Maharashtra facility.The regulator raised concerns about the products’ composition and whether they qualified to be sold as rum.The unlisted company’s revenue from operations dropped 64% to Rs 288 crore during April-September, compared with Rs 792 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier, according to its latest financial results. The contraction was even steeper in the September quarter, with revenue falling 77% year-on-year to Rs 108 crore from Rs 473 crore.The sales restrictions were imposed after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) inspected the company’s manufacturing facility in Khopoli, according to an ET report..The regulator objected to the use of neutral spirit blended with rum flavouring, contending that such products could not be marketed as conventional rum and should instead be classified as rum-flavoured spirits.It also raised objections to product descriptions such as ‘7 Years Old Blended’ and ‘Very Old Vatted’.The facility has remained shut since May, according to the financial daily.Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries, the company that is responsible for manufacturing and bottling Old Monk in Maharashtra, challenged the FSSAI order before the Bombay High Court.However, it withdrew its petition on November 5, informing the court that it would submit revised labels directly to the regulator for approval. The court disposed of the petition as not pressed, leaving the sales restrictions in place.Mohan Meakin had earlier agreed to drop the claim that the rum had been aged for seven years and make information about the addition of flavouring more prominent on its labels. The regulator, however, maintained that the central dispute concerned how the product itself should be classified.At an October hearing, the company’s lawyers told the court that the restrictions had resulted in losses of around Rs 50 crore for the company and deprived the Maharashtra government of nearly Rs 350 crore in excise revenue. They also said that about 300 workers had been left without work.The regulatory setback comes at a time when Mohan Meakin has been working to restore Old Monk’s market position following years of declining sales, as whisky has gained dominance in India’s liquor market.The brand, which is around seven decades old and has long been associated with winter drinking, hostel rooftops and military canteens, saw its annual sales volume decline to 4.1 million cases in 2013 from a peak of 8 million cases in 2002.Sales subsequently recovered, and two years ago, Old Monk overtook United Spirits’ McDowell’s No. 1 Celebration to become India’s largest-selling rum brand by volume. The brand sold 14 million cases in 2025.The turnaround followed a leadership change after Brigadier Kapil Mohan, the company’s long-serving chairman, died in 2018.
Article Summary: Mohan Meakin saw its revenue more than halve in the first six months of the current financial year. Food safety authorities stopped sales of three Old Monk variants which are produced at its Maharashtra facility. The regulator raised concerns about the products’ composition and whether they qualified to be sold as rum.

Article Title: No transactions made, no OTPs shared: Bengaluru techie loses Rs 5.5L in AMEX, RBL card fraud
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

Similar Crime:

One minute, three transactions: Man loses Rs 3.4L

How to stay safe

Disable international transactions: Keep international usage switched off unless required. Enable it only when making overseas payments.

Set transaction limits: Set lower spending limits for online, contactless and international transactions. Increase them temporarily when necessary.

Never share card details: Do not disclose your card number, CVV, expiry date, PIN or OTP to anyone, including people claiming to represent banks.

Avoid suspicious links: Do not click on links received through SMS, WhatsApp, emails or social media that promise rewards, refunds, credit card upgrades or fee waivers.

Do not install unknown APK files: Avoid downloading applications from unverified websites or links. Never grant unnecessary permissions to applications.

Avoid public Wi-Fi for payments: Do not access banking applications or make financial transactions through unsecured public Wi-Fi networks.





BENGALURU: A 31-year-old software engineer lost Rs 5.5 lakh in a credit card fraud involving his AMEX and RBL Bank cards on Nov 11, after cybercriminals allegedly carried out multiple unauthorised transactions within just an hour.According to the complaint filed by Siddarth (name changed), a resident of Indiranagar, fraudulent transactions worth Rs 4,02,722 were made on his AMEX credit card, while Rs 1,44,558 was debited from his RBL Bank card. The transactions took place between 12.56 pm and 2 pm, taking the total loss to Rs 5,47,280.Siddarth told police that neither he nor his family members had shared their card details, OTPs, PINs or other confidential banking information with anyone. He also denied downloading any APK files or authorising transactions.The family became aware of the fraud after receiving notifications about the suspicious transactions. Siddarth immediately contacted both banks, got the cards blocked to prevent further losses and reported the incident to the national cybercrime helpline 1930 before approaching police.A case has been registered at the East Cyber Crime police station under the Information Technology Act and Section 318 (cheating) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Why do such frauds happen?Credit card frauds involving unauthorised transactions can occur even when victims insist they have not shared their OTPs, PINs or card details. In many cases, fraudsters exploit weaknesses in digital payment systems, steal card information through sophisticated methods or misuse compromised credentials, the officer said.However, in this case, investigation will have to establish how the card details were accessed and how the payments were authorised, he added.Another senior officer said the possibilities of siphoning off money from credit cards include card data theft: Fraudsters may obtain card numbers, expiry dates and CVV details through compromised websites, data breaches, phishing links or fake payment gateways. Compromised online platforms: If an online shopping website, payment gateway or merchant account is compromised, stored card information may be exposed.Three back-to-back transactions within a minute cost a 30-year-old private firm employee Rs 3.4 lakh after fraudsters misused his credit card, which he claimed he had not used for the last five months. He received alerts for all three transactions together while he was on a phone call on Nov 6. He immediately contacted the card support team and reported the fraud.Rehman (name changed) from Lingarajapura said the transactions included Rs 1,36,996 at Innovative Retail Concept (BigBasket), Rs 39,200 at Php Indus Appstore Private and Rs 1,64,852 at Blinkit.He said he had neither made nor approved the payments; he had not received or shared any OTP.
Article Summary: A 31-year-old software engineer lost Rs 5.5 lakh in a credit card fraud involving his AMEX and RBL Bank cards on Nov 11. The transactions took place between 12.56 pm and 2 pm, taking the total loss to Rs 5,47,280. Fraudsters allegedly carried out multiple unauthorised transactions within just an hour.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), one of the most anticipated video games in recent years, to showcase India's economic and infrastructure transformation, drawing a comparison between the country's progress during the 13-year gap between GTA V and GTA 6."India is playing a whole new game!" Modi said in a post on X, sharing a series of colourful graphics styled around the popular Grand Theft Auto video game franchise.Titled 'Between GTA V and VI, here's how India upgraded', the graphics compare India's position in several sectors during the period between the release of GTA V in 2013 and GTA VI in 2026. The comparison covers economic growth, poverty reduction, sanitation, renewable energy and the space sector.The post uses the gaming franchise's long-awaited return as a reference point to present India's development over the past 13 years.One of the graphics compares India's economic position, describing the country as part of the 'Fragile Five' economies during the GTA V era and portraying it as the world's fastest-growing major economy in the GTA VI era.The comparison reflects India's changing economic position over the past decade, with the country emerging as a major growth centre in the global economy.Another graphic focuses on poverty reduction, showing extreme poverty declining from 27% in the 'Then' category to 2.6% in the 'Now' category.The illustration contrasts a cluster of thatched houses with a modern home and a family, presenting the change as an indicator of improvements in living conditions.The graphics also highlight India's sanitation drive, showing sanitation mission completion rising from 39% to 100%.The comparison features children using dustbins and a public sanitation facility, alongside the Swachh Bharat Mission logo.The renewable energy sector is another focus of the post. The graphic shows India's solar capacity increasing from 2.82 GW to 175 GW.It contrasts workers installing solar panels with a large solar power installation, presenting the expansion of renewable energy infrastructure as another marker of India's transformation.The final comparison focuses on India's space sector and the growth of private participation in space technology.The graphic shows the number of space startups increasing from one during the earlier period to 440 in the present, depicting workers assembling a rocket in a modern manufacturing facility.The comparison reflects the expansion of India's private space ecosystem following the opening up of the sector to private players.Meanwhile, Congress on took a swipe at PM Modi after he invoked the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, or GTA 6, saying it was very appropriate as the video game follows a “criminal duo”.Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said, “The PM, in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth, has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media.”“Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate,” he said on X.An action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI was rolled out across the globe on Thursday, marking its entry into the GTA series following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V.PM Modi's post coincides with the global release of Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026, ending a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V was released in September 2013.Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA VI returns players to Vice City, a fictionalised version of Miami, and follows the story of protagonists Jason and Lucia. The game is launching on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.The long gap between the two instalments has made GTA VI one of the most anticipated entertainment releases, with Rockstar building expectations through trailers, promotional campaigns and pre-release announcements.By using the franchise's return as a timeline, Modi's post draws a parallel between the evolution of the gaming series and India's development across economic, infrastructure and technology sectors over the same period.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) to showcase India's economic and infrastructure transformation. He drew a comparison between the country's progress during the 13-year gap between GTA V and GTA 6. The post uses the gaming franchise's long-awaited return as a reference point to present India's development.

NEW DELHI: In a stinging rebuke, PM Modi on Thursday admonished the corporate sector for not passing on the benefit of reduced corporate tax to employees through higher wages or through more hiring because of their greed.New Delhi: In a stinging rebuke, PM Modi on Thursday admonished the corporate sector for not passing on the benefit of reduced corporate tax to employees through higher wages or through more hiring because of their greed."In 2014, the basic corporate tax rate was 30%. We reduced it to 22%. Today, there is no income tax on earnings up to Rs 12 lakh in India. I know you will not clap, because however much one gives, your appetite never seems to be satisfied. I have exempted income up to Rs 12 lakh from tax. Did you increase the salaries of your employees? Did you increase the number of employees? No. The attitude remains: 'Modiji, you do it, we will see'," PM said at the Ficci AGM. He said tax relief to individuals had helped boost consumption and govt had reduced GST rates and speeded up I-T refunds, freeing up money that was earlier stuck for months. The comments came amid fresh demands for tax sops in the upcoming budget with business leaders submitting their wish list to the FM.Businesses are citing cost pressure and weakening demand amid signs of a pick-up in investment.While PM Narendra Modi cited India's rapid growth, he also called upon industry captains to suggest more reform proposals. "I have come because I respect you. But your experience with previous govts has been so bitter that I am paying the price for it. This is not that old govt. This is a friendly govt... Without hesitation and without inhibition, write to me openly and tell me what reforms are still needed."While urging industry to think beyond the domestic market and produce quality products, he asked them "seize the opportunity" offered by the trade agreements that are being signed.At the same time, he reiterated his message to promote 'swadeshi', citing the call made by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, and flagged pharma, steel and aluminium among sectors for a domestic manufacturing push."Everyone is sitting here and knows this. India is known as the 'pharmacy of the world'. Yet, despite this, India imports APIs, bulk drugs, and drug intermediates worth billions of dollars every year. There are hundreds of such categories where we still depend on imports. Our pharmaceutical industry must understand which ingredients can be produced within India... We already have strength in finished medicines.Now we must also build capability in ingredients." He also called upon industry to step up investment in agriculture.Besides, he suggested that companies look beyond their comfort zone and enter areas that are strategic."Industry must also prepare for the demands that will emerge in the future at both the national and global levels. We must work on those capabilities that, in this era of weaponisation of resources, become all of our responsibility to secure the nation's future. Therefore, my request to you is this: in every long-term investment decision over the next 20 years, make 'India First' your foundation. This will make the country self-reliant and will also open new opportunities for the growth of your businesses. "
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi admonished the corporate sector for not passing on the benefit of reduced corporate tax to employees. He said tax relief to individuals had helped boost consumption and govt had reduced GST rates and speeded up I-T refunds. The comments came amid fresh demands for tax sops in the upcoming budget.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle-age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests.Under the new rules, notified on November 13, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity, while older vehicles will have to undergo emission tests at shorter intervals. The revised framework also standardises PUC certificate validity for older emission categories across the country, replacing variations in testing requirements between states.The changes have been introduced through the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, which amend Rule 115(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. The amendment came into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.Previously, the validity of a PUC certificate was determined primarily by the vehicle's Bharat Stage (BS) emission category. Consequently, a newly registered private car and an older commercial vehicle, despite belonging to the BS-VI category, were both eligible for a certificate valid for one year.The revised framework introduces a more differentiated approach for BS-VI vehicles. Certificate validity will now depend on two factors:The vehicle's age will be calculated from the date of its first registration.Under the earlier system, all private BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for 12 months, irrespective of their age.The revised rules introduce three validity brackets:This means owners of newer private BS-VI vehicles will have to undergo emission testing less frequently, while those with vehicles older than 10 years will face more frequent testing.Commercial BS-VI vehicles will also be subject to an age-based validity schedule, although the extension for newer vehicles will be shorter than that available to private vehicles.Previously, all commercial BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for one year. Under the amended rules:The revised schedule therefore offers longer validity to newer commercial vehicles, but retains more frequent testing requirements for older ones.The amendment also introduces a uniform testing requirement for vehicles conforming to older emission standards.Previously, BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles were generally subject to a six-month PUC certificate validity under the central rules. However, some states had prescribed shorter intervals. Delhi, for instance, already required these vehicles to undergo emission testing every three months.Under the revised framework, the validity period for all BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles will be three months, irrespective of their age or category.This makes the three-month testing requirement applicable uniformly across all states and Union territories.For BS-IV vehicles, the earlier central provision allowed a PUC certificate validity of 12 months. However, certain states and areas within the national capital region (NCR) had already imposed a shorter six-month validity.The amended rules now prescribe six months as the standard validity period for all BS-IV vehicles across the country, irrespective of whether they are private or commercial.The change effectively brings the national requirement in line with the stricter timelines already followed in some regions.The amendment also clarifies how the validity period of a renewed PUC certificate will be calculated, depending on when the vehicle owner undergoes the emission test.Renewal within 10 days before expiry: If the vehicle undergoes testing within the 10 days preceding the expiry of its existing certificate, the renewed certificate will take effect from the expiry date of the previous certificate. This ensures that owners do not lose any remaining validity by renewing early.Renewal on or after expiry: If the test is conducted on or after the existing certificate's expiry date, the renewed certificate will be valid from the date of the test.PUC certificates issued before the amended rules came into force will remain valid until their respective expiry dates.Vehicle owners do not need to obtain fresh certificates immediately to comply with the revised schedule. The new validity provisions will apply when they renew their existing certificates for the first time under the amended rules.For instance, a private BS-VI car that is four years old and currently holds a one-year PUC certificate will become eligible for a three-year certificate at its next renewal. The revised validity will not automatically extend the certificate it already holds.All vehicles must have a valid PUC certificate issued by a testing centre authorised by the respective state government.Under Rule 116 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, vehicle owners are required to produce the certificate when demanded by an authorised official. Its validity can also be verified digitally through the Parivahan PUCC Portal.Under the earlier provisions, new vehicles across emission categories were exempt from obtaining a separate PUC certificate for the first year following their initial registration. However, the available details of the latest amendment do not clarify whether this exemption has been altered or retained.
Article Summary: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle- age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests. Under the new rules, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity. Older vehicles will have to undergo tests at shorter intervals.

Article Title: SC: Assess buyer's liability before home loan recovery
Article Text:
NCLT or NCLAT cannot ask flat buyers to repay the financier without first examining the “unholy” bank-builder nexus, said SC

NEW DELHI: In a big relief to lakhs of homebuyers, SC has ruled that in housing projects that remained incomplete despite banks releasing major portion of loan instalments to rogue or insolvent builders, the commercial courts, NCLT or NCLAT cannot ask flat buyers to repay the financier without first examining the "unholy" bank-builder nexus.The order came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana on a petition by homebuyers in Krishna housing project, Gurgaon, by Raheja Developers, which has gone into insolvency proceedings.The petitioners said the bank had started recovery proceedings against them in a commercial court in Saket, New Delhi, even though they had not yet got their flats.The CJI-led bench said, "It is the bounden duty of the commercial court to determine the nexus between the builder and bank officials and to see whether the bank disbursed the loan amount to the builder strictly in terms of the tripartite agreement."It said unless a categorical finding is returned that the homebuyers are in default, no interim direction regarding payment of instalments can be issued. "We direct the civil court not to take any coercive action against the petitioners or similarly placed homebuyers without first determining the above-mentioned issue," it said.As per the tripartite agreement between buyers-builder-banks, the financier was to disburse the loan amount directly to the builder in proportion to the progress in construction on ground.However, in many cases, because of builder-bank officials nexus, the financial institutions released loan amounts against each flat buyer much more than the money that should have been disbursed to the builder given the stage of construction of the housing project.When the project remained incomplete for decades, the bank filed recovery suits against homebuyers who, without getting the flats, kept paying EMIs and house rent. A decree in the suit would mean fastening crippling financial liability on the homebuyers.In Sept last year, a Justice Kant-led bench ordered a CBI inquiry against a large number of builders and banks across India for colluding to misuse the tripartite subvention scheme and fleece the homebuyers even when the projects remained incomplete for decades.On Thursday, the bench found its sympathy for the homebuyers has virtually opened the floodgates of litigation and thousands of them suffering under the tyranny of builders and banks have rushed directly to SC. It said, "Our hands are full and we may not be able to handle fresh litigation."In a similar case from Bengaluru involving over 4,000 homebuyers, it protected homebuyers against possible recovery proceedings from banks as the housing project remained incomplete for nearly a decade despite the petitioners paying 95% of the cost of the flat. After granting protection, the bench asked the petitioner's counsel to move Karnataka HC for appropriate relief.
Article Summary: Commercial courts, NCLT or NCLAT cannot ask flat buyers to repay the financier without first examining the "unholy" bank-builder nexus. The order came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana on a petition by homebuyers in Gurgaon.

Article Title: Next door, worlds apart: India's child malnutrition puzzle
Article Text:
AI generated picture

Good news nationally, with a catch

India's fight against child malnutrition is showing progress, but not on every front. While fewer children are falling behind in height, weight-related problems remain stubbornly persistent.

Does living near a big city help?

India's latest child nutrition data reveals striking inequalities even between neighbouring districts

The districts that were carved out

What lies behind the gap

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A common refrain in India is that birth is a lottery, where a child is born can, in many ways, determine how their childhood is shaped, if not their entire life. But even children born in neighbouring districts may have very different courses in life. This interesting facet has emerged from an analysis of district-wise malnutrition data published in the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6).In Nagpur district, roughly one in five children under five is classified as stunted, or too short for their age under standard child-growth measures. In neighbouring Chandrapur, also in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, it is more than two in five. The latest survey puts childhood stunting at 20.2% in Nagpur and 42.4% in Chandrapur. The two neighbouring districts show remarkably divergent statistics.The previous survey makes the gap harder to explain. In NFHS-5, conducted in 2019–21, Nagpur's figure was 27.6% and Chandrapur's 37.3%. Since then, Nagpur's estimate has fallen and Chandrapur's has risen.In November 2025, TOI reported on a programme for 915 mothers and children through 27 Anganwadi centres in Chandrapur's Jiwati taluka. The people running it described low literacy, reliance on subsistence farming and little variety in children's food.It is a reflection on how authorities are trying to reverse the worrying trend.The World Health Organization links stunting to poorer learning and school performance, more frequent illness and lower wages in adulthood. The first 1,000 days, from conception to a child's second birthday, are particularly critical. Growth lost during this period can have lasting consequences. While some catch-up growth is possible, full recovery is often difficult.India has made a substantial gain against stunting, which reflects the effects of poor nutrition, repeated illness and other disadvantages over a child's early years. The national estimate fell from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6.Children's weight-related indicators have barely changed, though. Wasting — being too thin for one's height — went from 19.3% to 19%. Underweight prevalence, which reflects both long-term and more recent nutritional problems, remained nearly flat, going from 32.1% to 31.8%. Severe wasting did fall, from 7.7% to 5.2%. Put simply, fewer of India's children are now classified as too short for their age, but almost one in five is still too thin for their height.TOI compared published figures for 680 districts and single-district Union territories with usable estimates for all three principal measures in both rounds. In 235, all three percentages were lower in the newer survey. In 196, stunting was lower but wasting and underweight were both higher.Vidarbha is not an exception. In Madhya Pradesh's Malwa belt, Indore reports 22.8% stunting, against 38.6% in neighbouring Dhar. The share of underweight children is 30.8% in Indore and 53.2% in Dhar, where more than half of young children are underweight.In Maharashtra's Marathwada, Beed's stunting estimate is 24.8%, while Hingoli's is 43.1%. In Odisha's KBK region, the historically disadvantaged belt associated with Kalahandi, Balangir and Koraput, Kalahandi reports 26.9% and Rayagada 47.2%. The two districts share a boundary.Often, it appears to. Nationally, stunting is estimated at 23.9% among urban children, compared with 30.9% among rural children. Look at Nagpur or Indore, and the obvious explanation might be jobs, hospitals and markets. Lucknow, too, reports a lower figure than neighbouring Sitapur: 31% against 45.5%.Tamil Nadu, though, bucks the trend. Coimbatore has a major industrial city, yet its district stunting estimate is 28%, compared with 15.6% in neighbouring Tiruppur, itself an industrial centre. The same is true in Bihar. Patna district, which contains the state capital, records 42.7% stunting, more than neighbouring Vaishali's 36.1%. On the underweight measure, the pattern reverses: Patna's estimate is 29.8% against Vaishali's 36.4%. A district with a large city also includes the villages beyond it, and its average mixes both.Research backs up the complexity of this relationship. A study of more than 443,000 children using earlier NFHS rounds found strong associations between stunting and household resources and mothers' education. After accounting for other characteristics, urban residence on its own was not a consistent predictor in the later rounds. A family's circumstances counted for more than its address.The clearest example is in Gujarat, where an official report acknowledged that averages were hiding disadvantage.Until September 2007, Tapi was part of Surat. The old district combined Surat's large urban economy with remote tribal areas. A Gujarat government human-development report, published in 2015, said combining them in one statistical profile had obscured conditions in places needing more development attention. Tapi was created from five predominantly tribal rural talukas. At the 2011 Census, Scheduled Tribes made up about 84% of its population.In NFHS-6, the stunting difference is relatively small: 30.4% in Surat and 33.9% in Tapi. The gap shows up in weight. Wasting stands at 14.1% in Surat versus 26.9% in Tapi, where more than one child in four is too thin for their height. Underweight prevalence is 32.2% versus 43.9%.The same pattern appears where other districts were divided. Chhota Udaipur, carved out of Vadodara in 2013, reports 51.5% stunting, affecting more than half its young children, compared with Vadodara's 35.5%. Palghar, separated from Thane in 2014, reports 42%, against Thane's 29%. State government figures based on the 2011 Census put the Scheduled Tribe share at 37.39% in Palghar and 5.27% in the reorganised Thane district. Palghar itself spans the urbanising Vasai–Virar belt and remote settlements, so its average hides further differences within the district.In Haryana, Nuh was formed in 2005 from five blocks of the former Gurgaon district. The region had been receiving special development attention well before that: Haryana established the Mewat Development Board in 1980. Today, the stunting estimates for Nuh and neighbouring Gurugram are 46% and 21.6%. The survey's separate measure of adequate diets among children aged six to 23 months also shows a wide gap, at 8.1% and 19.6%.Mizoram has a similar case. Mamit was carved out of Aizawl district in 1998. The latest stunting figures are 41.2% in Mamit and 23.1% in Aizawl. The Mamit administration's 2011 Census profile identifies it as one of the state's least urbanised districts.NFHS-6 found that just 15.3% of children aged six to 23 months nationally met its standard for an adequate diet, based on a combination of food groups and feeding frequency. That is up from 11% in the previous survey. It still means more than eight in ten children at that age miss out on enough variety in their food, enough meals in a day, or both.Family circumstances show up clearly in the data. An analysis of NFHS-5 found stunting among about 46% of children whose mothers had no formal education, compared with 23% among children whose mothers had higher education — half the rate. Education overlaps with household wealth, maternal health and living conditions, so this is an association, and the separate effects are hard to untangle.There are limits to these comparisons. NFHS is not a census of every child, and its rounds do not follow the same children. District estimates have sampling uncertainty, which this analysis has not independently quantified. Research using earlier surveys has also found that the season of measurement affects wasting. Yet, as India looks to become more prosperous, the onus is on ensuring that none of the next generation falls through the cracks. That would be a big step towards becoming a developed nation.
Article Summary: India's fight against child malnutrition is showing progress, but not on every front. While fewer children are falling behind in height, weight-related problems remain stubbornly persistent. India has made a substantial gain against stunting, which reflects the effects of poor nutrition, repeated illness and other disadvantages over a child's early years.

NEW DELHI: Continuing to be the most populous country in the world, India’s population for 2026 is estimated to be 1.47 billion (147.66) crores with the population doubling time of 81 years, according to the UNFPA’s State of The World Population Report 2026 released on Thursday. India’s population is expected to grow to about 1.7 billion (170 crores) before it begins to fall, around 40 years from now.India’s population was 1.46 billion in 2025, 1.44 billion in the year before that. More than one in four Indians are aged 10 to 24, the report highlights citing it to be India’s “youth moment” and calling for investing while the dividend window is open.Surpassing China, India became the world’s most populous country with 142.86 crore people in 2023 with China falling behind India with a population of 142.57 crore.Meanwhile, China’s estimated mid - year population for 2026 stands at 1.41 billion (141.29 crores) with 70% of the population in the 15-64 years bracket. 15% of China’s population is 65 and above. Fertility rate stands at 1.0 and life expectancy is high at 76 for men and 82 for women.The demographic indicators show that in India those in the 0-14 years age group account for 24% of the population; for 10-19 years this is 17% and for 10-24 it is a strong 26% reflecting India’s youth dividend.The data shows that 69% of India’s population is in the 15-64 years bracket and the population aged 65 and older account for 8%.Life expectancy for males is 71 years and that for females is 74. If one looks at world population in 2026 it is estimated at 8.3 billion with population doubling time 84 years. Globally life expectancy at birth stands at 71 for men and 76 for women.The report, flags India’s Total Fertility Rate at 1.9, the same as last year, which is below the replacement level fertility of 2.1 births per woman indicating that women are having fewer children than needed to maintain the population size from one generation to the next.The 2026 report also draws on UNFPA’s global Demographic Futures Survey of more than 108,000 internet-connected adults in 73 countries, including 1,722 in India to highlight aspirations around relationships, parenthood and life goals, and the conditions that influence people’s ability to realise them.It further states that young people’s aspirations regarding family and relationships will play a central role in shaping the nation’s demographic trajectory.Survey findings from India show that optimism runs high with 83% of respondents feeling positive or very positive about the future, despite concerns about conflict, economic insecurity and inequality, UNFPA highlights. Women aged 18 to 39 describe an ideal family size of 2.1 children and parenthood remains a strong aspiration: nearly 85% of childless respondents aged 35 to 39 would ideally like to become parents.“Young people need confidential, non-judgmental ‘Sexual Reproductive Health’ information and services (contraception, menstrual health, STI prevention, referral) alongside pre-pregnancy, maternal and postnatal care,” UNFPA states while emphasising the need for India to expand and strengthen youth-responsive primary care.
Article Summary: India’s population is expected to grow to about 1.7 billion (170 crores) before it begins to fall, around 40 years from now. More than one in four Indians are aged 10 to 24, the report highlights citing it to be India's ‘youth moment’

Article Title: Malaysia to not remain visa free for Indian visitors from Jan 1, 2027
Article Text:
The decision comes after an increase in Indians misusing the visa-free entry for employment purposes.

NEW DELHI: Malaysia could, from Jan 1, 2027, withdraw its visa exemption policy for Indian visitors. The southeast Asian country had in Dec 2023 started this to boost tourism post Covid. While the immigration department of Malaysia announced last month “Indian nationals entering Malaysia from (Jan 1, 2027) onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa prior to their arrival,” the Malaysian High Commission in Delhi told TOI Thursday the “visa-free (visa exemption facility) period tentatively ends on Dec 31, 2026.” Which means unless that facility is extended, going to Malaysia will require a visa from next year.While there was a surge in Indians visiting the country, the High Commission of India (HCI) in Kuala Lumpur had recently warned that there had been “a noticeable increase in Indian nationals arriving in Malaysia using the 30-day visa-free facility, to seek employment.” This, HCI had warned, “is a clear violation of immigration rules, as the visa-free entry facility which permits Indian passport holders to stay in Malaysia for up to 30 days is granted for tourism and social visits only.The immigration department of Malaysia (JIM) said in an announcement dated Nov 17, 2026: “…visa exemption facility for Indian nationals will no longer be available with effect from Jan 1, 2027. Accordingly, Indian nationals entering Malaysia from this date onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa prior to their arrival. Visa applications may be submitted through the MyVISA portal starting Dec 1, 2026.” Other countries whose citizens require visa to enter Malaysia include Bangladesh, Bhutan, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal.The Malaysian High Commission in New Delhi told TOI Thursday: “Currently all Indian passport holders are allowed to enter and stay in Malaysia for up to 30 days only (for each entry) without any visa for tourism, business or social visits purposes. This Malaysia visa-free (visa exemption facility) period tentatively ends on Dec 31, 2026. Therefore, Indian Nationals entering Malaysia from Jan 1, 2027, onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa before arrival. ”Going visa free for Indians in Dec 2023 had led to Malaysia seeing a spike in visitor numbers from here. From just over 7.3 lakh Indian tourists in pre-Covid 2019, the number rose to 13.6 lakh in 2024; 15.6 lakh in 2025 and 7.4 lakh in Jan-June 2026 with a target of 21 lakh for this full calendar year.However, HCI, Kuala Lumpur had in a X post on Sept 22, 2026, warned against the misuse of tourist visas. “…Many Indian nationals are misled by unscrupulous agents with false job promises, leading to overstay, illegal status, exploitation, detention and legal action. This is a clear violation of immigration rules…. Genuine tourists must carry valid and verifiable documentation such as confirmed return ticket, hotel booking, online submission of the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) three days before the arrival date, and a passport with minimum 6-month validity, to avoid any immigration-related issues on arrival in Malaysia.Once again, Indian nationals are strictly advised not to travel to Malaysia for work / employment purpose without work permit or visa with reference (VDR),” the HCI post had added.The Malaysian immigration dept announcement of Nov 17 adds: “…all visa processing fees paid are strictly non-refundable, regardless of the application outcome, change of policy or any subsequent change to travel plans. JIM reserves the right to amend these entry requirements at any time in accordance with directives from govt of Malaysia.”
Article Summary: Malaysia could withdraw its visa exemption policy for Indian visitors from Jan 1, 2027. The decision comes after an increase in Indians misusing the visa-free entry for employment purposes. The southeast Asian country had in Dec 2023 started this to boost tourism post Covid.

Article Title: Centre moves to tighten controls on antibiotic manufacturing, bulk drug trade
Article Text:
Representational image

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a move to tighten oversight of the pharmaceutical supply chain and tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR), the Centre has proposed stricter controls on both the manufacturing and wholesale distribution of antibiotics and other bulk drugs. Under the proposed changes, fresh manufacturing licences for antimicrobials will require prior central approval, while wholesalers dealing in bulk drugs, including active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), will need a separate licence to improve monitoring of their movement.In a draft notification, the Union health ministry has proposed amending the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to include antimicrobials in the definition of a 'new drug'. This would require manufacturers seeking fresh licences to first obtain permission from the Central Licensing Authority (CLA) before approaching state licensing authorities for a manufacturing licence. Existing manufacturing licences will remain valid and will not require fresh central approval.The ministry's move follows concerns that antimicrobial manufacturing licences are being granted without adequate quality checks, including bioavailability, bioequivalence and stability studies.The proposed central scrutiny is aimed at ensuring the quality and efficacy of medicines, as substandard or ineffective antimicrobials can contribute to drug resistance and make infections harder to treat.Antimicrobial resistance occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites develop resistance to medicines used to treat infections, making treatment more difficult and increasing the risk of prolonged illness, complications and deaths.Separately, the ministry has proposed a separate application form and licence for bulk drug wholesalers under the Drugs Rules, 1945. Currently, a common wholesale licence covers both bulk drugs and finished medicines. The new framework will require sales to be supervised by a competent person and licences to specify the categories of bulk drugs handled, including those covered under the NDPS Act. The move aims to improve tracking, curb diversion of controlled substances and strengthen oversight of bulk antibiotics amid AMR concerns.The two proposals are part of the Centre's broader efforts to strengthen drug regulation and promote responsible antimicrobial use through a One Health approach, recognising the links between human, animal and environmental health.Both draft amendments are open to public and stakeholder comments before finalisation and are not yet in force. While the proposed manufacturing approval requirement will apply to fresh licences, existing bulk drug wholesale licence holders will get time to comply with the new requirements, which will take effect after expiry of their current retention period or 12 months from the final notification, whichever is later.
Article Summary: The Centre has proposed stricter controls on both the manufacturing and wholesale distribution of antibiotics and other bulk drugs. Fresh manufacturing licences for antimicrobials will require prior central approval. wholesalers dealing in bulk drugs, including active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), will need a separate licence.

Article Title: Medicines may face tighter checks from factory to pharmacy under new Centre proposal

Medicines could face tighter quality checks not just at manufacturing units but throughout their journey to pharmacies and patients, with the Centre proposing to bring Good Storage and Distribution Practices (GSDP) under the Drugs Rules, 1945.The Union health ministry has proposed incorporating GSDP guidelines into the rules to ensure that the quality, safety and efficacy of pharmaceutical products are maintained from the manufacturer or importer to the point of supply to patients.The proposed framework seeks to cover every stage of the distribution chain, including procurement, purchasing, storage, transportation, distribution, documentation and record-keeping.The move is aimed at addressing risks that can compromise medicines after they leave manufacturing facilities, including deterioration due to improper storage conditions, contamination, mix-ups, falsification, diversion and unauthorised distribution.The guidelines, developed by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), are expected to strengthen inspections and enforcement by central and state drug-control authorities.They will also require greater documentation, traceability and accountability among manufacturers, importers, wholesalers, distributors, stockists and other entities involved in the pharmaceutical supply chain.The proposal seeks to ensure that medicines retain their specified quality and environmental conditions during storage and transportation, rather than relying solely on quality checks conducted at the manufacturing stage.The ministry has invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public on the proposed amendment.
Article Summary: The Union health ministry has proposed incorporating GSDP guidelines into the Drugs Rules, 1945. The proposed framework seeks to cover every stage of the distribution chain. The move is aimed at addressing risks that can compromise medicines after they leave manufacturing facilities. Article Title: Nepal PM Balen Shah's first India visit on November 23, talks with PM Modi on agenda
Article Text:
Nepal PM Balen Shah

Indian ambassador meets Balendra Shah ahead of visit

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will undertake a two-day State visit to India from November 22 to 23 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi . The visit will include delegation-level talks, the inauguration of energy projects and discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation, Nepal's foreign secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai announced on Friday.A 34-member government delegation led by Shah will travel from Kathmandu to New Delhi for the high-level engagement, Rai said, according to news agency ANI. Shah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with PM Modi on Monday, November 23.Following the meeting, the two Prime Ministers will jointly inaugurate several energy-related projects. Bilateral agreements and other instruments covering different areas of cooperation will also be signed and exchanged, according to the announced itinerary.The two leaders are also scheduled to address a joint press conference, after which PM Modi will host a luncheon in honour of the visiting Nepali Prime Minister.During his stay in New Delhi, Shah will call on President Droupadi Murmu and pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at his memorial in Rajghat. He is also scheduled to attend the Nepal-India Business Forum, which is aimed at strengthening trade and economic ties between the neighbouring countries.A separate business delegation is also expected to travel to India alongside Shah and his official delegation.Shah received an invitation from PM Modi to visit India after his government, led by the Rastriya Swatantra Party, was formed in March. The government came to power around six months after youth-led Gen Z protests toppled the administration of former prime minister K P Sharma Oli in September last year.According to Nepal’s foreign affairs ministry sources quoted by news agency ANI, discussions during Shah’s visit are expected to cover rail, road and air connectivity, infrastructure development, cooperation, trade and tourism.The visit is also significant against the backdrop of the longstanding diplomatic convention under which newly elected Nepali prime ministers make India their first official bilateral foreign destination. However, the practice is not an absolute rule. Oli departed from the convention in 2024 when he chose China for his first official bilateral visit.Ahead of the visit, newly appointed Indian Ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela called on Shah on Wednesday and discussed preparations for the high-level engagement, the Indian Embassy in Nepal said in a statement shared on X.The embassy said Dalela conveyed PM Modi's greetings to the Nepali Prime Minister and briefed him on the preparations."Ambassador @SudhakarDalela called on Rt. Hon. Mr. Balendra Shah, Prime Minister of Nepal, today. Ambassador conveyed the greetings of Hon'ble PM Shri @narendramodi and shared details of ongoing preparations for the forthcoming high-level visit," the embassy said.It added that Shah thanked the Indian PM and the Indian government for the assistance extended to Nepal following the floods in the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi region."Rt. Hon. PM Balendra Shah conveyed his gratitude to Hon'ble PM Narendra Modi and the Government of India for the support extended after the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi flood," the embassy said.According to a readout from Nepal's Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, Shah also congratulated Dalela on his appointment and wished him a successful tenure. He enquired about the preparations for his India visit, while Dalela informed him that the agenda had been finalised.India and Nepal share close historical, cultural and geographical ties, supported by a 1,751-km open border and extensive people-to-people connections. The upcoming talks are expected to review bilateral cooperation, with energy, trade and economic engagement among the key areas on the agenda.
Article Summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will undertake a two-day State visit to India from November 22 to 23. NEW DELHI: In a relief for owners of newer vehicles, govt Thursday extended the validity of Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs) for private BS-VI vehicles up to six years old for three years against the earlier norm of one year. At the same time, it has tightened norms for older vehicles, requiring BS-IV vehicles to renew their PUCC every six months, compared to the earlier norm of one year, and BS-I to BS-III vehicles every three months, against the existing six-month interval.The revised norms, notified by road transport and highways ministry, came into effect from Thursday. “The validity of PUCCs for BS-VI vehicles has been extended considering that they emit fewer pollutants than older vehicles. The new norm will also act as a disincentive to keep older vehicles,” an official said.BS-VI vehicles emit up to 82% less particulate matter (PM) and 25% less nitrogen oxides (NOx) than vehicles complying with BS-IV emission standards.The official said frequency of PUCC testing has been graded according to vehicle age. BS-VI vehicles aged between six and 10 years will have to renew their certificates annually while those older than 10 years will need to do so every six months.For older BS-IV vehicles, both private and commercial, largely manufactured before March 2020, the renewal frequency has been increased to every six months, given their higher pollution potential.The notification has prescribed a different schedule for BS-VI commercial vehicles. Those up to six years old will need to undergo PUCC testing once every two years while vehicles older than six years will require testing every six months.It also clarifies that the revised validity norms will apply to existing vehicles only after their current PUCCs expire and they go for renewal. Vehicle owners will have to apply for renewal 10 days before the expiry of their existing certificates.The changes are part of the government’s plan to roll out a new PUCC 3.0 regime.Motor vehicle expert Anil Chhikara said BS-III and older vehicles will need more frequent PUC checks as they lack advanced exhaust after-treatment systems. “BS-IV and BS-VI vehicles have more advanced, sensor-based systems, but the six-month validity for BS-IV vehicles will ensure closer attention to their maintenance as they age,” he added.Chhikara added that the new norm may have limited impact if vehicles are not properly maintained. “A poorly maintained BS-VI vehicle can emit more pollutants than a well-maintained BS-IV vehicle. Govt should, therefore, encourage regular vehicle maintenance and reward those with lower emission levels. It should also make fitness tests mandatory for private vehicles, on the lines of commercial vehicles, to ensure they remain roadworthy and comply with emission standards. Such requirements are already in place in several countries,” he said.

The revised norms, notified by road transport and highways ministry, came into effect from Thursday.

Article Title: Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Yashwant Varma to Parliament
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Justice Yashwant Varma has maintained that he is innocent of allegations relating to the discovery of burnt currency notes at his official residence and asserted that his resignation as a High Court judge cannot be treated as an admission of wrongdoing or acceptance of the findings against him.In a letter dated September 10 to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh, circulated among MPs on Thursday, Varma argued that proceedings initiated for his removal had become infructuous following his resignation on April 9. He contended that any attempt to continue the removal process would have no constitutional basis.Citing Article 217(1)(a) of the Constitution and the Supreme Court's 1978 Constitution Bench judgment in Union of India vs Gopal Chandra Mishra, Varma argued that a High Court judge's resignation takes effect on its own and does not require acceptance by the President or any other authority."Upon my resignation, proceedings directed towards my removal from office did not survive and cannot be continued," he wrote.Varma said he had participated in the inquiry conducted by the Judges Inquiry Committee until April 9, when he submitted his resignation to the President with immediate effect. He also referred to objections raised over the manner in which the inquiry was conducted and said he reserved the right to challenge its findings.He declined to comment on the committee's report or participate in any further proceedings. He requested that his letter and its enclosures be placed before members of both Houses of Parliament and that the matter be closed.Inquiry committee found all three charges provedThe three-member inquiry committee constituted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla found all three charges against Varma proved in its report, which was tabled in Parliament on August 12.The committee examined allegations relating to the discovery of burnt and partially burnt currency notes at Varma's official residence in New Delhi following a fire during the intervening night of March 14 and 15, 2025.The first charge concerned Varma's failure to satisfactorily explain the presence, source and ownership of the cash. The committee held that substantial unexplained currency notes of Rs 500 denomination were found within the official premises occupied by him. It clarified that its finding did not require establishing that Varma personally owned the money in the criminal-law sense.The second charge related to the failure to secure and preserve material evidence. The committee found that the storeroom had not been sealed at the relevant stage and that the site was subsequently disturbed, resulting in the unexplained disappearance of the currency notes. It clarified that the finding did not establish that Varma personally removed the cash.The third charge concerned the explanations provided by Varma during the inquiry. The committee described them as "evasive, incomplete and misleading in effect", stating that his alternative theories, including allegations of conspiracy and possible involvement of other persons, were not substantiated by the material on record.How the controversy unfoldedThe controversy began on March 14, 2025, when burnt bundles of currency notes were discovered at Varma's official residence during firefighting operations following a fire.A Supreme Court in-house committee subsequently examined the allegations. Its findings of misconduct led then Chief Justice of India Sanjiv Khanna to recommend Varma's removal.Varma, who was then a judge of the Delhi High Court, was repatriated to the Allahabad High Court, his parent court. He took the oath there on April 5, 2025, but ceased to discharge judicial functions.Nearly 150 MPs subsequently moved a notice seeking his removal, following which the Lok Sabha Speaker constituted the three-member inquiry committee under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.Varma challenged the constitution of the committee in the Supreme Court, but his plea was rejected. He later withdrew from the inquiry, alleging that the process lacked fairness and due procedure. He had maintained that he was not in Delhi when the incident occurred and that no cash was recovered.He resigned on April 9 while the inquiry was underway. However, the committee proceeded with its investigation and submitted its findings to Parliament.The resignation has not yet been formally notified. Legal experts have maintained that Varma has ceased to be a judge despite the absence of formal notification and that Parliament cannot proceed with his removal.Under the Constitution, Supreme Court and High Court judges can leave office either by resignation or through removal by Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. The term "impeachment", commonly used to describe the removal of judges in India, does not appear in the constitutional provisions governing the process.
Article Summary: Justice Yashwant Varma has maintained that he is innocent of allegations relating to the discovery of burnt currency notes at his official residence. In a letter dated September 10 to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh, circulated among MPs on Thursday, Varma argued that proceedings initiated for his removal had become infructuous.

It could also seek his further custody if required, he added.Three applications were moved on behalf of Chandrakar during the proceedings. Two sought permission for him to sign affidavits in jail and meet his advocates in a room in the presence of jail authorities.The third sought a direction that no order be passed on any future production warrant or transit remand sought by the ED or another agency without first hearing the accused.The court gave the ED time to file its reply and fixed November 27 for the next hearing, Pande said.Chandrakar was extradited from Oman earlier this month following a CBI operation. He was produced before a special CBI court in Raipur on November 4. The court granted the agency eight days of custody and allowed it to take him to Delhi for questioning.After the CBI remand ended, he was sent to judicial custody. The ED subsequently arrested him and secured a seven-day custodial remand on November 13.While seeking his custody, the ED told the court that the alleged illegal operations of the Mahadev app and related money laundering were continuing. It estimated the total proceeds of crime at more than Rs 92,000 crore.Investigative agencies have alleged that Chandrakar and Ravi Uppal, both natives of Bhilai in Chhattisgarh's Durg district, promoted the Mahadev Book App with their associates. They allegedly operated an online betting network through multiple panels and branch operators.According to the agencies, the accused earned around Rs 450 crore a month from betting since the Covid-19 lockdown in 2020. Hundreds of bank accounts allegedly opened using forged documents were used to move the illegal money.Panel operators allegedly transferred betting proceeds to Chandrakar and other promoters in the UAE through multiple bank accounts.The CBI has also alleged that a large portion of the earnings was spent on advertising betting websites and organising lavish events. Celebrities were allegedly paid from these proceeds.The agencies have further alleged that police and administrative officials, along with influential political figures, received illegal financial benefits as protection money.Chandrakar and other promoters allegedly ran the syndicate from Dubai, which they considered their headquarters. Several youths from Chhattisgarh were allegedly recruited as managers, supervisors and other staff.The ED has alleged that Chandrakar left India in 2022 to evade the process of law and stayed abroad without joining the investigation.He came into the spotlight in early 2023 after photographs and videos of his lavish wedding in Dubai surfaced on social media. The event reportedly cost more than Rs 200 crore and was attended by several Bollywood celebrities.The case also triggered a political controversy ahead of the 2023 Chhattisgarh Assembly elections. Shubham Soni, another accused in the case, released a video alleging that he had paid a huge amount to then chief minister Bhupesh Baghel. Baghel denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated.According to police sources, the app began operations in 2017, with its user base growing sharply during the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020.
Article Summary: Saurabh Chandrakar is the alleged kingpin of the Mahadev online betting app case. He was sent to judicial custody till December 2 by a special court in Raipur. This comes after the Enforcement Directorate said it did not require further custodial interrogation at this stage.

Article Title: Is Asim Munir Pakistan's Gorbachev? Why he wants to divide Pakistan and what it means for India
Article Text:
Is mineral wealth another motive?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Why India should watch closely

WATCH THE FULL EPISODE OF FAULTLINE WITH SUSHANT SAREEN HERE:

Pakistan's proposed division into smaller provinces is being pitched as administrative reform. But strategic affairs analyst Sushant Sareen believes there is a larger political and financial agenda behind it.In an interview with me on Faultline on Times Axis Youtube channel, he argued that the Pakistan military wants to fragment the country's political landscape so that no political party can challenge its dominance.“It's not an army. It's a political party. It's like the Communist Party of China,” he said.Sareen believes the proposed restructuring could weaken Pakistan's major political parties, particularly the Pakistan People's Party in Sindh and the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz in Punjab.If Karachi is separated from Sindh, he argues, the PPP could lose much of its political influence.“If People's Party loses Karachi, there's no point running Sindh because Sindh without Karachi is nothing,” he said.The same dynamic, he believes, could play out in Punjab. Smaller provinces could weaken established political dynasties while creating opportunities for local leaders to become chief ministers.“It's better to become the chief minister of a smaller part of Punjab than be just a member of the provincial assembly or a minister in Punjab,” Sareen said.He believes the restructuring is being pushed by the military establishment rather than emerging from a genuine political or administrative process.“This is by diktat of a dictator, or a quasi-dictator, or an undeclared dictator,” he said.Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has suggested holding a referendum on the proposal. Sareen questioned whether a referendum could bypass the constitutional process for creating new provinces.He also warned that the restructuring could trigger political backlash, administrative confusion and instability.“If Asim Munir wants to be the Gorbachev of Pakistan, I'm the last person to stop him from doing that,” Sareen said.Sareen also pointed to concerns that the proposed restructuring could give the establishment greater control over the mineral wealth of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.He believes the military wants greater control over resources, while also seeking a larger share of Pakistan's revenues.The existing revenue-sharing arrangement gives provinces around 57 per cent of the divisible pool. Sareen argued that the federal government already receives the lion's share of the country's overall resources.“Greed has no limit,” he said.He believes the military's financial interests could be another factor driving the proposed restructuring.Would a reorganised Pakistan become more stable? Sareen doubts it.He believes instability in Pakistan could benefit India, but only if it remains controlled.“Instability in Pakistan is very good for us, but provided it's a controlled instability,” he said.An uncontrolled crisis in a country of around 250 million people could become a serious problem for India.The military's attempt to restructure Pakistan could therefore have consequences far beyond its domestic politics.
Article Summary: Pakistan's proposed division into smaller provinces is being pitched as administrative reform. But strategic affairs analyst Sushant Sareen believes there is a larger political and financial agenda behind it. Smaller provinces could weaken established political dynasties while creating opportunities for local leaders to become chief ministers.

Article Title: India, Italy target €20bn trade by 2029, explore economic corridor linking Asia and Europe
Article Text:
